test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 10 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

Jane was asked by her (aunt, "Where were you least night"?)

options.text: aunt that, "Where were you last night?"

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** error in** the sentence is the incorrect use of the word **'least' instead of 'last'.**
 
• The **proper sentence** should read: *"Jane was asked by her aunt, "Where were you last night?"*
 
• It's ideal to keep the quotation marks (") to denote direct speech and the comma (,) should immediately follow 'aunt' and precede the quotation.

Therefore, the** correct answer **is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'Option 1', **is incorrect because it suggests 'No substitution required' which is incorrect because the word 'least' has been wrongly used instead of 'last'.
 
• **'Option 2', **"aunt that, "Where were you last night?"" is incorrect because it includes the word 'that' which doesn't fit syntactically in the context of direct speech.
 
• **'Option 4', **"aunt, "Where last night you was?"" is incorrect owing to word order issues and non-standard English usage: "Where last night you was?" is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "Where were you last night?"
